scaling.natural: The value is already a 0-100 measure where 100 is best (share of population covered, WHO service coverage index); it is used as is.
scaling.world: 0 and 100 are set at the 5th and 95th percentile of every country's latest value worldwide (data/reference.json), worst to best, on a log scale for skewed rates. Scores are clamped to 0-100. Adding countries to the atlas does not move anyone's score.

not_yet_scored.reason: WHO's household-survey measures are missing or older than 10 years for many countries, and Europe and the rest of the world use different definitions. Shown on country pages, not scored.
Needs comparable data on gaps between income groups for every country.
Needs comparable waiting-time and unmet-need data beyond the EU and the Commonwealth Fund's 10 countries.
Shown separately as the score against spending per person, not folded into the score, so cost and performance can be read apart.

excluded_countries.TWN: Not covered by World Bank, WHO or OECD statistics; needs official Taiwanese data on the same definitions.
